subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Lab-Grown Organs: Engineering Replacement Parts
description: A 60-second lesson on Lab-Grown Organs: Engineering Replacement Parts.

hook.text: Over 100,000 people in the US await organ transplants. Lab-grown organs could eliminate the shortage entirely.

buildup.text: Tissue engineering grows cells on scaffolds — structures guiding cell growth into shape. The scaffold dissolves as tissue forms.

discovery.text: Simple organs like bladders and skin grafts are already grown in labs. Complex organs need vascular networks that are far harder.

twist.text: Pig organs modified with CRISPR have been transplanted into humans. In 2024, a pig kidney worked in a patient for over two months.

climax.text: Bioprinting layers living cells into organ shapes. A bioprinted liver isn't here yet, but miniature organoids test drugs today.

punchline.text: Grow it. Print it. Transplant it. No waiting list needed.

quiz.question: What role do scaffolds play in tissue engineering?
options: They provide nutrients to growing cells and replace the need for blood vessels
They guide cell growth into the correct organ shape and dissolve as tissue forms
They protect the new organ from the patient's immune system during transplant
